title: sessions: protect provider telemetry identifiers
body:
## What

Protects Agents window telemetry from connection-specific provider details without changing event cadence:

- maps sessions providers to the bounded `default-copilot`, `local-agent-host`, `remote-agent-host`, and `other` categories before emission;
- replaces raw `agentSessionId` values with deterministic SHA-1 hashes so events for one session remain correlatable without exposing provider or resource details;
- applies the same treatment to live session action events and persisted `agents/sessionSummary` rows;
- migrates persisted per-provider request counters into the same bounded categories so `userSessionsForProvider` remains consistent with the emitted provider dimension.

`providerType` remains unchanged as the useful low-cardinality session-type dimension.

## Why

Follow-up to [microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8738](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8738).

Remote Agent Host provider IDs include a connection authority. Aggregated production validation over seven complete UTC days found 49 distinct dynamic provider IDs, including address-like shapes. Every observed `agentSessionId` was prefixed by its raw `providerId`, so changing only `providerId` would leave the same connection detail in the correlation field.

The shared session-field builder feeds 23 Agents action events, and lifecycle summaries build the same fields separately. This change protects both paths.

## Query impact

- `providerId` is now a bounded category. Remote hosts intentionally aggregate under `remote-agent-host`.
- `agentSessionId` remains deterministic within the new population, but its value changes from the raw ID to a hash. Queries cannot join raw historical IDs to hashed new IDs across the deployment boundary.
- `providerType` retains the existing session-type breakdown.
- Existing persisted provider counters are aggregated into their bounded categories on first read and rewritten without dynamic provider keys on the next increment.
- Event names, cadence, and row counts are unchanged.

## Validation

- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\test\common\sessionsTelemetry.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\sessionsLifecycleTracker.test.ts` (33 passing)

title: agentHost: Rename provider telemetry to harness
body:
## Overview

### What

Rename the Agent Host telemetry discriminator from `provider` to `harness` and normalize the Copilot harness value from `copilotcli` to `copilot`.

The normalization is applied at telemetry boundaries only. Agent Host provider registration, session URI schemes, session types, routing, persisted state, and legacy Copilot CLI migration identities remain unchanged.

The change covers:

- Agent Host lifecycle, turn, tool, changeset, migration, instruction, and todo telemetry
- shared `languageModelToolInvoked` and edit telemetry fields populated only for Agent Host rows
- workbench Agent Host invocation failures and remote Agent Host provider-invoked telemetry
- Agent Host edit attribution and edit-survival telemetry

Unknown or custom harness IDs pass through unchanged. Copilot-only GitHub forwarding remains gated on the raw `copilotcli` provider identity rather than the normalized label.

### Why

The existing property identifies the Agent Host harness/backend, not the model or API provider. Calling it `provider` is ambiguous with model-provider telemetry elsewhere in the same events and codebase.

Production samples also show inconsistent Copilot labels: generic Agent Host events emit `copilotcli`, while Copilot compatibility events emit `copilot`. VS Code already uses `harness` for remote Agent Host and edit-attribution telemetry, so this change aligns the schema and value vocabulary.

Relevant history:

- #316797 introduced `agentHost.userMessageSent.provider`
- #311301 changed the internal Copilot routing identity from `copilot` to `copilotcli`
- #324278 introduced `harness` for per-harness Agent Host analysis

## Property-by-property parity

| Field | Previous source | New source | Parity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` / `harness` | Raw Agent Host provider/session scheme | Central telemetry normalization of the same raw value | ≈ Same harness signal; Copilot label changes from `copilotcli` or `copilot` to `copilot` |
| `agentSessionId` | Agent Host session URI | Unchanged | ✅ |
| Other event properties | Existing emitters | Unchanged | ✅ |

Normalized values:

| Raw provider ID | Telemetry harness |
|---|---|
| `copilotcli` | `copilot` |
| `copilot` | `copilot` |
| `claude` | `claude` |
| `codex` | `codex` |
| other values | unchanged |

## Measurement-by-measurement parity

No measurements, units, or aggregation formulas change.

- Event cadence, row counts, namespaces, and populations are unchanged.
- New rows use `harness`; historical rows continue to use `provider`.
- Shared events leave `harness` absent for non-Agent-Host traffic, matching the previous optional `provider` population.
- Queries spanning the cutover should coalesce the two fields and normalize both Copilot spellings:

```kusto
| extend harness = case(
    tostring(Properties['harness']) in ('copilot', 'copilotcli'), 'copilot',
    tostring(Properties['provider']) in ('copilot', 'copilotcli'), 'copilot',
    isempty(tostring(Properties['harness'])), tostring(Properties['provider']),
    tostring(Properties['harness']))
```
